preparation_rules: Clean thoroughly: Wash multiple times in cold water to remove sand, silt, and tiny shells caught in broad fronds.
Short cooking times: Delicate sheets overcook quickly and become mushy; add at the end of hot dishes or flash-dry.
Dehydration for seasoning: Oven-drying or sun-drying intensifies umami and turns the leaves into a versatile flake/powder topping.

recipes.title: Traditional Irish Sea Lettuce & Potato Soup
recipes.description: A velvety potato soup finished with vibrant fresh sea lettuce leaves for a rich, mineral ocean depth.
ingredients: 150 g fresh Ulva lactuca (sea lettuce, washed and chopped)
500 g Yukon Gold potatoes (peeled and diced)
100 mL heavy cream or whole milk
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse Ulva lactuca fronds in cool water to clear sand and grit. Drain well and chop into ribbons.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté onion and garlic until soft and translucent.
Add diced potatoes and stock to the pot. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in chopped sea lettuce and simmer for just 3 to 5 minutes so it retains its bright green color.
Remove from heat, stir in cream, and blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.title: Crispy Baked Sea Lettuce Chips
recipes.description: Light, paper-thin savory sea chips baked from whole Ulva lactuca fronds.
ingredients: 100 g fresh Ulva lactuca fronds (whole sheets)
1.5 tbsp extra virgin olive oil or sesame oil
1/2 tsp fine sea salt or garlic salt
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C (250°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wash sea lettuce sheets thoroughly, then pat completely dry using paper towels or a salad spinner.
Gently toss dried fronds with olive oil, sea salt, and sesame seeds in a bowl until lightly coated.
Spread fronds in a single layer on the baking sheet without overlapping.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until dry and crisp. Let cool completely before serving as a snack.

recipes.title: Japanese Aosa Miso Soup (Sea Lettuce Miso Soup)
recipes.description: A classic coastal Japanese miso soup featuring tender sea lettuce added right before serving.
ingredients: 50 g fresh or rehydrated Ulva lactuca
4 cups dashi stock (kelp and bonito broth)
3 tbsp dashi-infused miso paste (red or white)
instructions: Rinse fresh sea lettuce in cold water and drain well. Slice into bite-sized pieces.
Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add cubed silken tofu and simmer for 2 minutes.
Ladle a cup of warm dashi into a small bowl, whisk in the miso paste until smooth, then pour back into the pot.
Turn off the heat, stir in the fresh sea lettuce and green onions, and serve immediately.
